note: A comprehensive literature review of 28 individuals with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome found visual impairment in 18/28 (64.3%), which is below 70%.

evidence.text: A literature review of 28 patients with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome revealed that visual impairment was present in 18 of 28 patients (approximately 64.3%), supporting the observation that ophthalmologic abnormalities are not present in all cases.

source.title: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome: Exploring a novel GTPBP2 mutation and a literature review
source.quote: Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28).

evidence.text: Phenotypic analysis suggests that some aspects of GTPBP2-associated clinical presentation appear to be age-related, indicating features like retinal dysfunction or neurodegeneration may not be fully penetrant in early childhood.

source.title: Clinical delineation of GTPBP2‐associated neuro‐ectodermal syndrome: Report of two new families and review of the literature
source.quote: Our findings suggest that some aspects of the clinical presentation appear to be age-related; brain iron accumulation may appear only after childhood, and the ectodermal findings and peripheral neuropathy are most prominent in older individuals.
